claim: Drifting fog banks roll sideways with real front-to-back depth — clean, soft-edged cool grey-white fog, not a flat wash.

q1_defects.answer: ROUND-2 RE-FIX VERIFIED: the hard rectangular square-tile grid from round-1 is GONE. Every play frame and every control frame now shows smooth, continuous, organic fog swirls with no axis-aligned seams and no checkerboard cells. I looked specifically for hard horizontal/vertical tile boundaries and found none in any frame. bandingScore reads ~0.29 on the dense play frames, but per the known over-report on high-detail organic fog swirls this is the desired wispy detail, not banding — the frames themselves contain zero hard square seams. No misalignment, cut-off, or low-contrast issues; the fog fills the viewport frame cleanly.
evidence: metrics: play-2 bandingScore=0.287 (organic-swirl over-report per caveat; LOOKED — no hard tile seams in frame)

q2_reads_as.answer: Reads clearly as clean, soft-edged cool grey-white fog with real front-to-back depth, exactly as claimed. Bright billowing wisps in the foreground sit over darker grey recesses, giving smooth volumetric falloff rather than blocky stepping. Hue is neutral grey-white (effSat=0), correct for cool fog and not a colored or warm wash. Strong luminance variation (stdev ~48) means it is NOT a flat wash.
evidence: metrics: play-2 effSat=0 effRGB=[144.8,145.3,144.6] (neutral cool grey-white), stdev=47.7 (depthful, not flat)

q3_discoverable.answer: Yes. The Density slider gives an obvious, sensible response a first-time user would read instantly: low = thin/dim fog, high = thick/bright dense fog. Layers low->high adds depth and structure, and Speed drives the sideways drift. All three labeled sliders map to intuitive results.
evidence: control: density low->high meanLuma 27.8->78.3, changed=true (visible thicken/brighten)

q4_responsive.answer: Responsive, not janky. The three play frames clearly differ — the fog has drifted/evolved between them — and control-apply latency is sub-600ms.
evidence: metrics: play-1 frameDeltaMag=2.99, play-2=3.3, play-3=8.61 (visible motion)

q5_net.answer: A user would be PLEASED: 'That's proper drifting fog now — soft, deep and clean, no more wall of grey square tiles.' The round-1 stone-wall checkerboard is fully fixed and it reads as volumetric cool grey-white fog with working controls.

flags.note: bandingScore stays near 0.29 on the dense play frames — harmless here (organic-swirl over-report, no visible tile seams) but it sits close to the 0.25 numeric threshold, so future automated checks shouldn't read that number as a regression.
flags.evidence: metrics: idle bandingScore=0.289 (organic detail, not banding)
